quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: What do double solid yellow centerlines mean?

options.text: You can pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot pass other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is slippery when wet.
There is a steep downgrade ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to dangerous conditions ahead. This sign tells you to drive carefully because the road may become slippery when wet.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?

options.text: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can cause carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes dangerous fumes from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: When driving near a motorcycle, what must you do?

options.text: Let the motorcycle use a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder next to the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half a lane.
Pass the motorcycle using the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the motorcycle use a full lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles with the same rights as other vehicles. Give them a complete lane width. They need space to move safely, even if there seems to be room to share.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a multi-lane intersection, but oncoming traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross are clear before turning.
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and safe.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line on a road mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed here if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed here if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed yellow line means you can cross it to pass if the way is clear. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: How can you prevent your vehicle from being hit from behind?

options.text: Drive faster than surrounding traffic to create more distance.
Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
Drive slower than surrounding traffic for better control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as surrounding traffic.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of traffic around you, within the legal limit. Driving with traffic flow prevents rear-end collisions and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Signal and communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do unexpected things. Communicate with other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when needed.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public highway?

options.text: Yes, as long as you are not driving.
Yes, if you are in the back seat.
Yes, if you are in the back of a pickup truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in any vehicle on a public road or sidewalk. You cannot store open alcohol containers in the front or back of a vehicle on any public road.

questions.question: A train has just passed and you are stopped at a railroad crossing. What should you do?

options.text: Look and listen for another train. Cross only if the tracks are clear.
Assume no other trains are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look and listen for another train. Cross only if the tracks are clear.
questions.explanation: When the last car of a train passes, do not move until you are sure no train is coming on another track. Check both directions. Only cross when you are certain the tracks are clear.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing. This gives other drivers time to know your plans in advance.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. Other drivers must be able to see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: You pass your destination while driving in heavy traffic on a city street. What should you do?

options.text: Back up to where you should have stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive around the block.
questions.explanation: Circle around the block to reach your destination. Never make a U-turn in heavy traffic as it disrupts traffic flow.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe speed for driving your vehicle?

options.text: A speed that is reasonable and safe.
A speed that fits current road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must not drive faster than is reasonable and safe. Adjust your speed based on traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and lighting. You must also stay within legal speed limits.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, intersections, or railroad crossings. These are unsafe and illegal places to pass.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians cross first.
questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. However, first check that no pedestrians or other vehicles are still in the intersection. Yield to them before moving.

questions.question: How can you safely drive after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Wait for some time to pass.
Drink black coffee or another caffeinated drink.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for some time to pass.
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, fresh air, food, or a cold shower might make you feel more awake, but they do not reduce alcohol's effects. You must wait for the alcohol to leave your system.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT happen when you drink alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time become slower.
Your ability to judge speed and distance becomes worse.
You stay calm and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You stay calm and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, makes it harder to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks. It does not help you concentrate.
